reason: README Quick Start CLI runs the OCR pipeline with small PP-OCRv5 models that work on CPU.
demo: README Quick Start > CLI Usage: paddlex --pipeline OCR ...
goal: Install PaddlePaddle (CPU) and PaddleX from the repo clone (with the OCR extras needed), then run the README OCR command: `paddlex --pipeline OCR --input <image> --use_doc_orientation_classify False --use_doc_unwarping False --use_textline_orientation False --save_path <dir> --device cpu`. It must download the models, recognize text in a local image with printed English text, print the result with rec_texts, and save result image/JSON files to the save path.
check: The hidden test runs the OCR CLI on a generated image of printed text on CPU and verifies the saved output files and that the recognized text contains the expected words.

revision.by: fairness review (every maintained-set exam re-checked against the source)
issues: Recognition check is vacuous: `tr A-Z a-z < log.txt | grep -q paddle` matches PaddleX's own log output (model names/paths under ~/.paddlex, 'PaddleX' messages) whether or not the image text was recognized; the 'rec_texts' grep only shows the key was printed. v2 reads rec_texts from the saved <stem>_res.json and requires both generated lines.
Pipeline exit status is ignored (no pipefail); v2 sets pipefail.
evidence: oracles/paddlepaddle-paddlex.sh:22-23 - grep 'paddle' over the whole CLI log
